finding.title: Split completion_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, and completion_dao_extended_test.dart under the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: All four are more than 2x the 400-line hand-written-file cap. completion_dao.dart mixes cross-profile-scope-guarded reads, raw-SQL tier filtering, and grouped aggregates in one file; points_balance_dao.dart mixes balance/ledger/redemption CRUD with sync-outbox plumbing; track_dao.dart mixes lifecycle CRUD with two different multi-table transactional delete flows. Long files raise the odds that the next edit misses a nearby invariant (e.g. the DB-3 loop found in track_dao.dart's purgeHistory, buried 400 lines in).
finding.recommendation: Split by responsibility, e.g. completion_dao.dart into a read/aggregate DAO plus a cross-profile-guarded companion; points_balance_dao.dart into balance+ledger vs redemption vs sync-enqueue helpers; track_dao.dart into lifecycle CRUD vs the two delete/purge transactional flows.
acceptance_criteria: A Rule-0 line-count check (e.g. `find lib -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) is added to `make audit` and passes.

finding.title: Narrow and log the catch-all in CompletionRepositoryImpl._appendStreakEvent

evidence.quote:
} catch (_) {
      // Defensive: never let a telemetry tee block the primary write.

finding.why: catch (_) swallows every exception from BOTH the streak_events Drift insert and the outbox enqueue (facade.enqueueStreakPayload) with no AppLogger call anywhere in this file — a codec bug, closed-DB race, or genuine corruption is indistinguishable from the expected benign duplicate-key case this comment is defending against. This is also EH-4-adjacent (catches Error subtypes, not just typed Exceptions) and evades the Rule-0 'no empty catch blocks' Makefile grep (`catch\s*(_\?\w*)\s*{}`), which only matches a literal same-line `{}` — this multi-line comment-only body is functionally empty but textually invisible to that checker. Per the file's own header comment, the outbox enqueue here is what 'closes the gap' where a second device sees a frozen streak; if enqueueStreakPayload throws, that gap silently reopens with zero diagnostic trail and no retry.
finding.recommendation: Catch a specific expected type (e.g. the Drift unique-constraint exception) for the benign-duplicate case and let everything else propagate or be logged via AppLogger.instance.warning/error before swallowing, so a genuine failure is at least visible in Crashlytics/Talker.
acceptance_criteria: The catch narrows to the specific expected exception type; every other path logs via AppLogger before returning; a regression test that makes enqueueStreakPayload throw asserts the failure is logged, not silently dropped.

finding.title: Split the four hand-written files in core/sync/merge that exceed the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.rule: AG-3 (hand-written Dart file <=400 lines; generated exempt)
finding.why: drift_merge_store.dart alone blends the LWW clock-skew gate, seven distinct per-entity upsert implementations, FK/account resolution logic and schedule JSON encoding in one file — the 'God File' shape AG-3's cap exists to prevent — and it is this batch's #1 churn hotspot, so every fix wave re-reads all 788 lines for context. The three oversized test files mirror the same sprawl.
finding.recommendation: Split drift_merge_store.dart into one file per upsert group behind the existing MergeStore interface; split drift_merge_store_test.dart/mergers_test.dart/notification_settings_merger_round_trip_test.dart to mirror, no behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: AG-3 line-count checker (grep/lint over lib/ and test/, generated files exempt) passes for all four files.

finding.title: Collapse duplicate equality/hashCode/toString assertions inside delta_value_test.dart

evidence.quote:
test('equality: not equal to different type', () {
      expect(const DateDelta(5) == const PaceDelta(5), isFalse);

test('equality: DateDelta != PaceDelta with same numeric value', () {
      expect(const DateDelta(5) == const PaceDelta(5), isFalse);

finding.why: Within this single 290-line file, several test() blocks are byte-for-byte identical in body under different names — e.g. lines 27-29 and 31-33 both assert `DateDelta(5) == PaceDelta(5)` is false; lines 39-41 and 47-49 both assert DateDelta(5).hashCode equality the same way; lines 51-53 and 55-57 both assert DateDelta(7).toString() contains '7'. Harmless (both copies pass and are correct) but purely additive noise: roughly 6 of the file's ~50 tests contribute zero incremental coverage over their twin, inflating the file for a future reader trying to find what's actually pinned.
finding.recommendation: Delete one test from each identified duplicate pair, keeping the more descriptively-named one.
acceptance_criteria: No two test() bodies in the file are textually identical (grep/diff check).

finding.title: Replace unchecked e.message as String? casts in PIN dialogs with a null-safe read
finding.why: ArgumentError.message is typed Object? in dart:core, not String?. Both sites hard-cast it with `as String?`, which would throw a TypeError if PinService ever threw an ArgumentError constructed with a non-String message (e.g. ArgumentError.value(...)). Today PinService only ever throws `ArgumentError('PIN must be exactly 4 numeric digits')` so this never fires, but the cast is a landmine for the next caller of setProfilePin/setTutorPin-style methods that doesn't preserve that convention.
finding.recommendation: Use `e.message?.toString() ?? <fallback>` instead of the unchecked cast in both places.
acceptance_criteria: Both sites read e.message without an unchecked String cast
A test constructing ArgumentError.value(42, 'pin') and feeding it through does not crash
